summary.headline: Fairchem Q1 FY27 revenue rose 34.4% YoY to Rs 176 crore and EBITDA margin reached 10.14%, driven by price realisation.
summary.overview:
Revenue from operations was Rs 176 crore, up 34.4% YoY, with EBITDA of Rs 18 crore (10.14% margin) and net profit of Rs 10 crore. Management attributed the gain mainly to higher price realisation, linked to elevated raw material costs, lower imports amid Middle East supply disruption, and reduced Chinese dumping. Sales volume was 13,500 tonnes versus 13,000 tonnes in Q1 FY26, while utilisation is near 60% against a target exit of 70-75% for FY27. Isostearic acid remains small (4% of revenue) with slow customer qualification.</overview>

segments.name: Dimer acid
segments.commentary: Approximately 30% of Q1 FY27 revenue; key export product alongside Isostearic acid.

segments.name: Linoleic acid
segments.commentary: Approximately 42% of Q1 revenue and about 40% of volume; goes into the paint industry.

segments.name: Isostearic acid
segments.commentary: About 4% of Q1 revenue; sold into cosmetics, qualification slow as only three global manufacturers exist.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q2-Q4 revenue and margin run rate to be maintained at current levels.
Capacity utilisation to rise by about 5% per quarter, to about 70-75% exit FY27 from roughly 60% now (on 80,000 tonne capacity).
A new oleochemical product is to start trial runs from Q2 FY27 on a 40,000 tonne capacity; ramp-up only after stabilisation; management says margins should be better than current.
Isostearic acid expected to exceed 80% capacity utilisation in 1-2 years; management indicated a positive outcome by end FY27 at some customers.
Export share currently 7-8% of revenue; management expects export growth from dimer and Isostearic acid, aided by India-UK and India-EU FTAs and rupee depreciation.
Management is not planning debt-funded or aggressive expansion given business risk.
capex_capacity: Current capacity is 80,000 tonnes; utilisation near 60% now, targeting 70-75% exit FY27.
A new 40,000 tonne oleochemical capacity is slated to begin trial runs in Q2; any capacity beyond 80,000 tonnes depends on this.
Energy conservation last year cut power consumption by more than 30% and solid fuel consumption by more than 35%.
Bypass fat plant and Isostearic acid (green route, third globally) are recent commissioned products.
demand_pricing: Price realisation up ~30% vs Q1 FY26 and ~25% vs Q4 FY26; management says raw material cost increases were passed through due to Middle East supply constraints and lower imports.
Management attributes improvement to reduced Chinese dumping, which it says may return and cannot be controlled.
Management says 7-8 large customers have enquired about alternative supply due to diversification.
Management declined to commit to long-term volume contracts with fixed pricing given volatility.
Paint industry is about 40% of revenue; management does not intend to reduce this dependence.
Duty inversion: raw material duty 16.5% (earlier 27.5% from 2024) vs finished product 7.5%, a roughly 9-point margin drag per management.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the revenue impact of the inverted duty structure versus dumping on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 9-point duty differential (16.5% on raw material vs 7.5% on finished product) is the margin loss; it declined to size the dumping effect and said the company is too small to influence duty policy.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin improvement sustainable if supply constraints ease?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company cannot control renewed dumping; it called sustainability uncertain and cited business risk as the reason for avoiding debt-funded expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What is R&D spend as a percentage of sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about Rs 50 lakh is spent on revenue R&D, with the CFO stating 1-1.5% of sales; the company will check the annual report disclosure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Isostearic acid outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said approvals from cosmetics buyers in Europe and Japan are slow; the company is at step 3 or beyond everywhere and expects a possible positive outcome by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Realisation change and sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation up about 25% from Q4 FY26 and about 30% from Q1 FY26; management hopes it holds as long as the West Asia crisis continues.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company sell at maximum utilisation now?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is happy with realisations and aims to reach 100% utilisation before ramping capacity further, with market share gains as the focus.

risks_watch: Renewed Chinese dumping or easing of Middle East supply constraints could reverse the pricing gain; management said it cannot control this.
Inverted duty structure (16.5% on raw material vs 7.5% on finished goods) continues to cost about 9 points of margin.
Isostearic acid qualification in cosmetics is slow; volume ramp is uncertain.
Paint sector concentration at about 40% of revenue and linoleic acid at about 42% of revenue.
Utilisation ramp to 70-75% depends on geopolitical conditions; the 40,000 tonne new product is undisclosed in end market.

Several answers were evasive (end market of the new oleochemical product, pricing magnitude of the tailor-made linoleic acid, dimer market size) and the R&D disclosure in the annual report was missing.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the near-term margin and realisation gains, but guarded and evasive on product details, end markets, pricing magnitude and the sustainability of Chinese import conditions. Management repeatedly declined to quantify or name customers.
key_quotes: Basic problem has been we have been always explaining that the duty structure on the raw material what we buy is 22.5% and the finished product carries 7.5% duty.
We are not going to manufacture anything for EV battery. We have never said that.
Quantities are going down; prices are going up.
